A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Alignment Score study. All pages, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original cross-model alignment scores, chain-selection accuracy, LLM-judge evaluations, ablations and qualitative cases in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds evaluations of Qwen3-4B-Instruct, GPT-5-mini and GPT-5 in Appendix E, Table 6.

M1.justification: Equations 1–6, Algorithm 1 and the ACSS/SC-Align selection procedures remain unchanged. The reference-curation revisions concern experimental input preparation, without introducing a new scoring or chain-selection component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same stated 1,024-question ScienceQA/ARC-Challenge coverage and 1–4-hop settings, with MATH, GPQA and MMLU comparison scores. The additional models use existing coverage; Reflexion and ReAct are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: CoT, SC-CoT and the alignment-based selectors retain their comparator membership, including in the new Table 6. The three judges and three NLI backbones are also unchanged. Additional evaluated language models are experimental configurations, not new competing selection methods.

E3.justification: Appendix D substantially revises the reported reference-preparation protocol: coherence-weighted ranking using three criteria and top-chain selection becomes two-criterion filtering on a 1–10 scale above 8.50, followed by author screening. v3 also specifies randomized reference generators and adds three evaluated model configurations. These are documented protocol revisions; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: The control-group case changes its question, SC-Align reasoning and conclusion, removing the earlier contradictory conclusion. The other three cases remain substantively intact. The existing judge/backbone grid moves from Appendix E to F without new ablation results.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeded runs and mean±standard-deviation reporting. v3 explicitly mentions LLM-evaluation scores in Appendix A.2, but v2 already applies this practice to all experiments, including ablations. No additional runs or uncertainty-estimation procedure is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes Qwen2.5/LLaMA2 MATH scores from 0.07/0.01 to 0.76/0.28 and correlations from 0.79/0.81/0.85 to 0.88/0.83/0.87. New Table 6 adds three-model results with mixed accuracy effects: GPT-5 SC-Align scores 96.72% versus SC-CoT's 96.81%, despite higher alignment. Tables 2–5 and the judge grid retain identical values. Case 1 changes its output, and all four cases lose numerical judge ratings.

T1.justification: The entropy, divergence and alignment-error definitions remain unchanged, as does Section 4.3's reasoning-depth argument. No theorem, proof or substantive mathematical correction is added.

C1.justification: v3 elevates readability and coherence associations into the abstract and contribution summary, and explicitly claims that optimizing Alignment Score improves these qualities in the conclusion. v2's corresponding summaries emphasize accuracy. The metric, sampling-method and two-hop claims remain.

C2.justification: New Section 5 discusses possible applicability to Reflexion, ReAct and agent trajectories, with additional segmentation requirements for branching structures. Ethical Considerations adds reference-style and judge-bias limitations and rejects interpreting high scores as guarantees of correctness or safety. Appendix D clarifies that author checks are not human preference labeling.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link and specifies reference generators, over 15,000 candidates, roughly 2,000 filtered chains and the 8.50 cutoff. Conversely, it removes v2's Python and AMD EPYC/A100 hardware disclosure. Most prompt and decoding details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds G-Eval, MT-Bench-101, Reflexion, ReAct and agent-system references, while removing citations including JudgeLM, Zheng et al. (2023) and Cover and Thomas. The new discussion broadens positioning toward agent trajectories; the principal comparisons with REVEAL, CoTKG and semantic-entropy research remain.

P1.justification: v3 corrects grammar and method-name inconsistencies, revises the abstract, contribution summary, conclusion and reference-curation prose, and adds discussion, ethics, acknowledgments and an experimental appendix. The main methodological and experimental narrative remains organized similarly.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains explicit example chains and revised curation labels. v3 adds Table 6, relocates Figure 3 with an expanded caption, and reformats the qualitative cases into more compact prose boxes. The existing judge table becomes Table 7; Figures 3–4 retain identical plotted content.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves numerical consistency through Table 1 correlations that match the displayed data, adds model comparisons, and clarifies interpretation limits. These gains outweigh the loss of hardware details and numerical case ratings. Reproducibility remains imperfect: revised reference preparation is not linked clearly to retained results, and the claimed generator/evaluation separation conflicts with GPT-5 appearing in both roles in Appendices D and E.
